title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement:
Given two sorted arrays A of size M and B of size N, find their median (the middle value of the merged sorted sequence).

If the total number of elements (M+N) is odd, the median is the single middle element. If even, the median is the average of the two middle elements — but since all elements are integers, print both middle values separated by a space if even (lower then upper), or just the median if odd.

**Approach**: Binary search on the smaller array to find the correct partition.

Complexity: O(log(min(M,N))).
constraints:
1 <= M, N <= 10^5
-10^9 <= A[i], B[j] <= 10^9
Both arrays are sorted in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers M and N.
Line 2: M space-separated integers (sorted array A).
Line 3: N space-separated integers (sorted array B).
outputFormat:
If (M+N) is odd: one integer — the median.
If (M+N) is even: two integers separated by a space — the two middle elements (lower then upper).
